mutant.description: SIX controls, and the run's whole design is adversarial. (1) A4 IS THE CONTROL FOR THE THREE REFUSALS: without a served answer on the same ticket, three 403s are consistent with a dead route or a wrong path. (2) The payloads were written and READ BACK with assertions before any call, so the constructed caller is on record rather than described. (3) A1 versus A2 tests whether firm plays any part in the refusal. (4) A2 versus A5 tests whether an existing ticket is distinguishable from a missing one. (5) The refusal bodies were scanned for a ticket id rather than trusted to carry none. (6) The before/after reads of ItemCount, status and events LENGTH test that five GETs wrote nothing, rather than assuming a GET cannot write. Plus: the IAM simulate was run on ONE resource ARN with the function's existence established FIRST, because an allowed on a resource that does not exist proves only that the pattern matched.
mutant.expected: (1) A4 200. (2) five payloads, five keys each. (3) identical. (4) identical. (5) none. (6) all three unchanged.
mutant.observed: (1) A4 served 200 with 27 ticket keys and status completed, consistent with the table's own before-read of the same ticket. (2) all five read back with version 2.0, method GET, exactly five authorizer keys, no body, no query string. (3) A1 and A2 identical in status, error, action and class -- refused by class, not by firm. (4) A2 and A5 identical in all four -- an existing and a missing ticket are indistinguishable to a client. (5) names_a_ticket false on all four refusals. (6) ItemCount 27 to 27, status completed to completed, events length 3 to 3. The simulate read allowed for lambda:InvokeFunction on the function's ARN, taken after reading the function's ARN from the live service.

determinism.method: ONE pass of five calls, as the pair bounds it -- no arm was repeated and no sixth call was made. Determinism here is therefore not a re-run but the independence of the record from the act: every payload was fixed on disk before its call, every answer was taken from the function's own returned object with its AWS invoke status and FunctionError flag recorded beside it, and the served A4 answer was cross-read against a ConsistentRead of the same ticket in DynamoDB.
determinism.observed: All five invocations returned AWS StatusCode 200 with no FunctionError, so no answer is a crash or a truncation. A4's ticket.status reads completed and the table's own projection read of that ticket reads completed before and after -- two independent planes agreeing on the one value the run is allowed to keep. No throttle occurred, so the pair's one permitted retry was not used. Branch E did not arise.
